bluf: Razorfish is a Publicis Groupe digital agency, founded 1995, New York based, selling brand experience, loyalty CRM, creator programmes and media to enterprise brands under the line leaders in what's next. It pitches itself as an AI era first mover with a CMO guide to AI visibility, while its own sitemap shows nothing updated in 12 months and it runs 0 Google ads. The Horus read puts it Neutral at 0.3, best placed for KJ4 and KJ8, most exposed to KJ6. A rival should know 11 of its 21 named clients are names only and HBO Max, Dove, Marriott Bonvoy, PayPal and Stellantis already sit on other tracked books.
doing:
Razorfish positions as leaders in what's next, blending predictive intelligence, cultural instinct and creative execution so brands move first in the AI era, with loyalty at the core: in plain words, a holdco digital agency selling brand, loyalty and media experience to large consumer brands. The headline claim is that it helped shape the internet era and now helps iconic brands move first with AI. The record lists founded 1995, owner Publicis Groupe, HQ New York, no employee count, and offices from New York and Los Angeles through Mexico City and Bogotá to London, Gurgaon, Mumbai and Sydney.

No line leads. Three score 2 as core: Creator & Influencer (the Creator CoLab platform, a Trojan TikTok creator case, a Chief Social & Innovation Officer), Email & CRM (a CRM & Loyalty practice under a Chief CRM Officer, Stellantis and Marriott Bonvoy loyalty cases) and Programmatic & CTV (a Media Experience practice led by a President and Head of Media, a connected media segmentation case). Ten lines score 1 with no evidence note, paid search, paid social, SEO and AI search among them; CRO and local score 0. The service menu spans Integrated Brand Experience, GenAI & Emerging Experiences, Customer Data Platforms and Mobile Applications; proprietary items are Creator CoLab and Beta Lab.

Its AI posture is framing rather than product: an AI era first mover with GenAI experiences and a CMO guide to AI visibility, while AI search and AI automation score 1 with no evidence. Dated moves are thin: news runs from 2020-10-28 to 2023-02-15, the one move is a 2025-03 Drum interview at SXSW marking its 30th anniversary, and the SXSW 2024 and Gen Alpha pieces carry no date; a news URL on Publicis Groupe relaunching Performics MercerBell to Razorfish is undated too. No pricing signals, jobs or ATS are listed. Conspicuously absent for a holdco digital agency: any partner badge, any dated case study, and a headcount.
clients:
Client type: enterprise; verticals: Automotive, Beauty & personal care, Banking & financial services, Travel & hospitality, Media & entertainment, Retail & pharmacy, Consumer technology and Museums & attractions; home market the US.

The needs read holds 21 clients: 10 observed and 11 names only; the mix is brand and creative (N3, 4), CRM and owned audiences (N6, 3), social and creators (N8, 2) and web build (N4, 1). No case carries a date. HBO Max came for a rebrand (an identity crisis turned into a content strategy). Dove came for social: Project #ShowUs (stock photos of real women and nonbinary individuals) won a silver Global Effie. Stellantis came for CRM (how can CRM feel more VIP) and Marriott Bonvoy for loyalty; Ram is coded CRM from a truck slug. Trojan came for creators through Creator CoLab; Alfa Romeo for brand work; Porsche for an engine notes concert; Pantone for a color match app; the Batiste launch sits under the fragment Effective and Creative Product.

Names only, need inferred from the core lines: PayPal, Samsung SmartThings, First Hawaiian Bank, Waldorf Astoria Miami, Cadillac, Bank of the West, Australian Centre for the Moving Image, Orangetheory Fitness, World of Coca-Cola, Patrón and Viviscal; Cadillac, First Hawaiian Bank, Bank of the West and ACMI carry excerpts the read did not code. Five sit on other tracked books: HBO Max (media-monks, phiture), Dove (media-monks, billion-dollar-boy), Marriott Bonvoy (code-and-theory, instrument), PayPal (lseo) and Stellantis (webranking).

What the base needs next, tied to KJ8 (human provenance as a distribution signal) and KJ4 (platforms absorbing execution): it is likely, moderate confidence, that these brands ask for creator programmes with visible human provenance and loyalty data that survives platform automation, and unlikely, low confidence, that they ask Razorfish for AI visibility work it has not evidenced.
house: Say and do: 2 lines tested, 1 practised, integrity 50. Creator work is corroborated by its own Instagram channel. Publishing cadence is contradicted: a blog exists but nothing in its sitemap of 211 URLs has updated in 12 months, 0 in 90 days and 0 in 365, and every blog date the deepen pass found is empty. It runs no Google ads, 0 in the Transparency Center, while listing Paid Search & SEM as a service. LinkedIn advertising is active: 24 company ads on the first results page, a floor because more pages exist, pushing Gen Alpha and loyalty research; one reads 'Marketers have long treated repeat behavior as loyalty. Our latest research says otherwise.' The tag stack is GTM alone on a Nuxt site; no social pixel, test tool or ABM stack detected. No llms.txt, no AI crawler blocked, 2 AI related URLs in the sitemap, for an agency publishing a CMO guide to AI visibility.
market:
The Horus read puts Razorfish at a tailwind index of 0.3, band Neutral, percentile 21, 16:28 on the Solar Arc. Best placed for KJ4 (platforms absorbing the execution layer) through Data & Measurement, with little paid execution to lose, and KJ8 (human provenance becomes a distribution signal) through Creator & Influencer and Content & Digital PR. Most exposed to KJ6 (the agency middle is being hollowed out) at a net of -0.717 through Paid Search and Paid Social, and KJ5 (attention prices split in two) through Programmatic & CTV. Best fit: The Commons Rebuilt, 47/100. Partial on P1 and P7, absent on P2, P6 and P8; P3 and P4 not applicable, P5 unknown.

The Monsoon read is 51.1, band Breeze, percentile 32: migration 64.6 against displacement 37.6. The mix supplies 43 of the index, Email & CRM (6) and SEO (6) carrying most movable hours; work goes 62% to South and Southeast Asia and 31% to Latin America. Footprint observed: hub offices in Mexico City, Bogotá, San José, Gurgaon and Mumbai (12 hub points, 10 holdco). No onshore claim.
openings:
The strongest judgment is the idle house against the first mover claim: Razorfish sells itself as an AI era first mover with a CMO guide to AI visibility, yet its sitemap shows nothing updated in 12 months, no llms.txt, 0 Google ads and no dated case study. A rival that shows a dated AI visibility result for a consumer brand very likely (moderate confidence) wins the first mover argument. Falsifier: a next compile showing sitemap updates in the last 90 days and an llms.txt on razorfish.com closes it.

The shoppers are the contestable accounts: HBO Max (media-monks, phiture), Dove (media-monks, billion-dollar-boy), Marriott Bonvoy (code-and-theory, instrument), PayPal (lseo) and Stellantis (webranking), and the 11 names only rows are a question for its clients. KJ6 at -0.717 hollows out the middle it occupies; migration at 64.6 with hub offices in Latin America and South Asia gives an onshore delivery pitch something concrete to point at, while displacement at 37.6 says the book does not buy on price, so lead with provenance and loyalty proof, not rate. No public pricing model (P5 unknown) and no feed or entity work (P2 absent) leave an outcome priced, machine readable offer unanswered.

I7, holiday 2026 agentic checkout volume and merchant opt out rates, December 2026 to January 2027: disclosed AI checkout GMV would speed KJ4, where it is best placed, and high Shopify opt out rates would slow it.

I6, platform AI labeling enforcement after the EU Article 50(2) deadline, 2 December 2026: new reach penalties for unlabeled AI personas or engagement would strengthen the KJ8 tailwind behind its Creator CoLab line.
